Every word of law in this repository comes from these sources. Lexifina reads them and records each act's dated versions, and the laws that made each change, in one corpus file. This repository is built from that file.

## Dates

Each commit is dated at noon (America/Sao_Paulo) on the day the change took effect. The other dates, enacted and published, are trailers.

When a law gives no date of its own, the default rule applies: Decreto-Lei 4.657/1942 (LINDB) art. 1: unless it says otherwise, a law takes effect 45 days after its official publication. This record takes in only state laws whose own vigência clause says they take effect on their publication (or signature), and dates each by the Diário Oficial date its ALESC page records (else by its date). https://www.planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/decreto-lei/del4657compilado.htm

## How the history is built

`tools/build.py` turns the corpus into this history in one pass: one commit per law, on the day it took effect. The same corpus always gives the same commit hashes. `tools/check_repo.py` reads every version back from git and compares it with the corpus. `tools/on.py` shows the law as it stood on any date. The corpus format is described in `tools/SCHEMA.md`.

- Corpus: sha256 `30d2ad165809b2a91c0f68e14bda8e0f4f726bb511fd886fa83b8643460d79c0` (56347757 bytes).

## Decisions made by hand

- Each state law ("Lei" and "Lei Complementar", including those promulgated by the Assembleia) still in force is given once, from ALESC's page for it as copied by the Internet Archive. A law whose page shows no later change is given as enacted, credited to itself and dated by the Diário Oficial date the page records (or, when it has no vigência clause, 45 days after it: LINDB art. 1). Any other law is given as the text in force on the page (struck earlier wordings and the publisher's alteration notes left out), credited to ALESC as the oldest version available and dated by the day the Internet Archive copied the page; its earlier wordings are not reconstructed yet.
- Left out: laws the page marks as repealed or declared unconstitutional as a whole, and pages without the ALESC layout, a heading carrying the record's number, an article or a closing line.
- The text runs from the law's heading through its closing line (place and date); the page's header block (Procedência, Natureza, DO, Fonte and its list of changes) and the signatures are left out. One file per Art.; "000-titulo" holds what comes before the first article.
- Each state law ("Lei" and "Lei Complementar", including those promulgated by the Assembleia) still in force is given once, from ALESC's page for it as copied by the Internet Archive. A law whose page shows no later change is given as enacted, credited to itself and dated by the Diário Oficial date the page records (or, when it has no vigência clause, 45 days after it: LINDB art. 1). ## What AI did and did not do

The scripts that read the sources and build this repository were written by Claude Code running Claude Opus 5.5 (`claude-opus-5-5`) under Lexifina's direction.

No model wrote, translated or corrected legal text. No model runs at build time. Every word of law in this repository comes from the official sources above.

The commit messages are written by `build.py` from the source data.

Model use at data-build time:
- Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5) wrote Lexifina's code and chose the sources. No model output is used as legal text or dates: every word comes from ALESC's pages.
